clue.text: Present man without eating food

indicators.note: the word for without swallows the food, so the food sits inside it

parts.note: sans is French for without, used in English
a pie is an item of food

explanation.surface: Someone today goes hungry, refusing to eat a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Homo sapiens is the species of humans living now, hence 'Present man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the species name for modern humanity, the man of the present.

clue.text: Poisonous to swallow carrot top? I doubt it

indicators.note: the poisonous word takes in the other letter

parts.note: septic means infected or poisoned

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that a toxic carrot top is safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a doubter, one whose response is that he doubts it.

clue.text: Take chair at piano and stay there?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to reside somewhere is to stay or live there

explanation.surface: A pianist is invited to sit down at the instrument and remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to chair a meeting, sitting in the position of authority.

clue.text: Praise for previous payment not complete

parts.note: ex means former or previous

indicators.note: the payment loses its last letter

parts.note: a toll is a payment for passage

explanation.surface: Commending someone for a debt only partly paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Sent round American money to be supportive

indicators.note: the word sent goes round the other pieces

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Dollars posted to someone as help.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustinent is a rare word for sustaining, giving support.

clue.text: Handy man first entering wine with no head

indicators.note: the first piece goes into the beheaded wine
the wine loses its opening letter

parts.note: Chablis is a white Burgundy wine
I is the Roman numeral one, so first

explanation.surface: A useful odd-job man gets into the wine before anyone else, ignoring the frothy top.
explanation.walkthrough: Homo habilis means 'handy man' in Latin: an early human species, here passed off as a handyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo habilis, the early human species, takes its Latin name from the meaning handy man.

clue.text: A large number — about 50 — planets are mine

indicators.note: the large number goes round the numeral

parts.note: a host is a great crowd
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An astronomer or miner boasts of owning a horde of worlds.
explanation.walkthrough: Gustav Holst composed the orchestral suite The Planets, so he can say they are his.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Holst wrote the suite The Planets, so he could claim those pieces as his own.

clue.text: Hogs (Bible revealed) that went racing down steep slope

definitions.text: that went racing down steep slope

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are opened out and laid in a new order

explanation.surface: The Gadarene swine of the Gospels rushed down a steep bank into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the possessed swine ran violently down a steep place; 'revealed' rearranges HOGS BIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobsleigh is a racing sled that speeds down a steep icy run.

clue.text: Picture crazy — O for a lunatic!

indicators.note: crazy says the letters are jumbled
one letter takes the place of the other in lunatic

explanation.surface: An image of madness, with a cry of lament for a madman.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the A of LUNATIC for an O, giving LUNOTIC, and 'crazy' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a design cut in linoleum, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Heliotropic grass surrounding international organization

indicators.note: the grass goes round the organisation

parts.note: sward is an expanse of grass
the UN, the United Nations

explanation.surface: Lawn plants turning towards the sun around a world body.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliotropic plant turns towards the sun, so grows in that direction.

clue.text: Man standing before court (the Guardian)

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
the newspaper speaking of itself says we, so us

explanation.surface: A man stands up in court before the newspaper's reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Homo erectus is Latin for 'upright man'; the clue appears in the Guardian, so 'the Guardian' speaks as US.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo erectus is the early human species whose Latin name means upright man.

clue.text: Veto breaking sign to north country

indicators.note: the veto breaks into the sign, splitting it open

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
to veto something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A ban breaks out under a northern star sign over some country.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a country in the Middle East on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Register of cases shows one hoping to play for his country

definitions.meaning: a ... is a court's schedule of cases to be heard

definitions.text: one hoping to play for his country
definitions.meaning: a player given a trial for a national team

explanation.definitionFit: A court list of trials and a sportsman on trial for selection share the same spelling.

clue.text: Saint of island that was mapped?

definitions.text: Saint of island that was mapped?

parts.words: Saint of island that was mapped?
parts.note: the island named after a saint appears on maps of the Caribbean, and the saint's name is what is wanted

explanation.surface: A question about which holy figure an island charted on maps is named after.
explanation.definitionFit: St Lucia, the Caribbean island, takes its name from the virgin martyr Saint Lucy, whose Latin name it carries.

clue.text: A number — a lot — worth little

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a heap means a lot, as in heaps of time

explanation.surface: A whole pile of items that are not worth much.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap costs little money, so is of low value.

clue.text: 9's dog?

parts.note: Peking Man was a Homo erectus, the 9 across species, so his dog would be named after his home city

explanation.definitionFit: The Pekingese is a toy dog breed from China named after the capital Peking.

clue.text: I came back with a boy all skin and bone

indicators.note: the words I came are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before the turn
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone returns with a lad who is painfully thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To be emaciated is to be extremely thin, wasted to skin and bone.

clue.text: Manx primate's time todie, possibly of love

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an ape is a primate
hr is short for hour, a time

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of todie may be another arrangement

explanation.surface: A tailless primate's hour to die, maybe for love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TODIE into ODITE. Aphrodite was the Greek goddess of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite was the Greek goddess of love, the deity described by these words.

clue.text: Sailor and boat — I would string them up

parts.note: Jack, or jack tar, is a familiar name for a sailor
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A hangman threatens to hang a seaman together with his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch was a notorious seventeenth-century English executioner whose name became a byword for the hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Ketch, the English executioner, became a stock name for any hangman, who strings people up.

clue.text: 9 translated agreement to put Mum in front

parts.note: ja is yes in German and Dutch

indicators.note: Mum is put inside the word for the front

parts.note: the van is the front of an army, the vanguard
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A foreign pact puts mother at the head of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 across is ERECTUS: Java Man is the fossil Homo erectus found in Java.
explanation.definitionFit: Java Man was the first Homo erectus fossil ever found, on the Indonesian island of Java.

clue.text: Foppish fellow to steer horse round mountain

parts.note: to cox is to steer a rowing boat

indicators.note: the horse goes round the mountain

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy horse
M is short for mountain on maps

explanation.surface: A dandy rows past while riding a horse round a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, showy man, a fop.

clue.text: Sound article more like 1 across than 5 across or 9?

definitions.text: more like 1 across than 5 across or 9

parts.note: a hum is a low sound
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Asking whether a spoken word is closer to one early man than another.
explanation.walkthrough: Modern man (1 across, SAPIENS) is more human than the earlier HABILIS (5 across) and ERECTUS (9).
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is fully human, while the older species were less so, so this adjective fits the comparison.

clue.text: Pitman fighting a deity?

parts.note: a pitman is a coal miner
v, versus, means against, as in a fight

explanation.surface: A coal worker takes on a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Trevor has queen (unknown) in place of sisters

parts.note: Trevor Nunn is a famous British theatre director
ER, Elizabeth Regina
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A theatre director sits with royalty in a home for nuns.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Trevor Nunn directed the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a convent, where religious sisters live.

clue.text: Earth mother's ecclesiastical title taking in 9

indicators.note: the title holds the number inside it

parts.note: Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A mother goddess bears a churchman's honorific that includes a number.
explanation.walkthrough: A fox's den is called an earth, so a mother living in an earth is a female fox. Here '9' is simply the number, not the cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A vixen is a female fox, and a fox's burrow is known as an earth.

clue.text: Sing about great start for man (early 1 across)

indicators.note: the word for sing goes round the other piece

parts.note: to croon is to sing softly
the start of Latin magnus or magna, meaning great

explanation.surface: Someone sings softly about a fine beginning for humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Cro-Magnon man was an early form of Homo sapiens (1 across) in Europe; MAGN is the opening of the Latin for great.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon people were early modern humans of Ice Age Europe, an early form of our own species.

clue.text: Approximate temperature of fiddle

parts.note: c, circa, means approximately
heat is a level of temperature

explanation.surface: Roughly how hot a violin gets.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a swindle or fraud, and to fiddle is to cheat.

clue.text: Vintage car owned by technical visionary

indicators.note: the car is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An old motor belongs to an engineering genius.
explanation.definitionFit: Alvis was a British car maker whose models are prized vintage cars.

clue.text: Poor income, little energy and no people at this time

indicators.note: poor signals the word income is in bad shape, rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Low earnings and little energy leave nobody about these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Miocene epoch ended millions of years before any humans walked the earth, which is why the definition says nobody was around then.
explanation.definitionFit: The Miocene is a geological epoch long before human beings evolved, so a time with nobody.

clue.text: With lines or the opposite?

definitions.meaning: ... means written in lines of poetry
the ... of something is its opposite

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means in poetry; as one it means reversed or contrary.

clue.text: Number those in heaven, the poshest or the best?

parts.note: the blest are the blessed souls in heaven

explanation.surface: Asking whether the saints are counted among the upper class or simply the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblest describes both the highest-born, the poshest, and the most excellent in character.

clue.text: City slicker's first in support of drug

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for support

parts.note: a stay is a support or prop

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of slicker

explanation.surface: A smooth City operator supports a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is the street name for the drug MDMA.
